To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Polish investors, who have decided to establish a subsidiary abroad through greenfield investment or acquisition, have a different impact on the competitiveness of their parent company, depending on the mode of entry into the host market.
the impact of Polish investors’ FDI on their competitiveness depends on the mode of entry (greenfield investment or acquisition).

the impact of FFI on investor competitiveness in terms of the main competitors operating in the home country market and on foreign market is different depending on FDI entry modes (greenfield investment and acquisition).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of FID entry mode (green field vs. acquisition) on competitiveness of the Polish companies.
the impact of foreign establishment mode choice on the competitiveness of investing Polish enterprises.

the relationship between the mode of foreign investment entry (greenfield vs. acquisition) on the one hand and the competitiveness of Polish FDI investors in their home and foreign markets on the other.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of FFDI on investor competitiveness depends on the FDI entry mode.
Polish investors who have entered foreign markets via acquisition are more likely to be competitive than those who have chosen a greenfield entry mode.
Polish investors who choose the acquisition entry mode have more chances to improve their competitiveness than investors who decide to establish a greenfield investment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Polish FDI companies have the greatest impact on their competitiveness when choosing greenfield investments.

Polish investors who choose greenfield investment as the FDI entry mode have the greatest impact on their competitiveness, which is reflected in the improvement in their position in relation to the most important competitors operating on the domestic market and in foreign markets.
Polish investors who have decided to enter foreign markets through acquisition have a better competitive position than investors who have decided on a greenfield investment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FDI companies operating on the home and foreign markets are more competitive than those operating only on foreign markets, and the difference is significant.
the impact of FFDI on competitiveness of investing companies depends on their entry mode (green field investment or acquisition).
the impact of FID on competitiveness of the investing company depends on the entry mode choice.
